title: Bigoli in Salsa
subtitle: Venetian whole wheat pasta with anchovy and onion sauce
excerpt: Bigoli in salsa is one of the most ancient Venetian pasta dishes: thick whole wheat spaghetti dressed with a sauce of slowly cooked onions and anchovies dissolved in olive oil. The onions and anchovies melt into an almost-black, intensely savoury paste that coats the rough pasta. Simple, cheap, and deeply good.
sourceNotes: Bigoli in salsa is a traditional Venetian fasting dish, eaten on the eve of Christmas, Good Friday, and the feast of the Redeemer. The dish is documented from the seventeenth century. Bigoli are a traditional Venetian whole wheat pasta made with a bigolaro, a press that extrudes the pasta. Thick whole wheat spaghetti is the standard substitute.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The anchovy-onion sauce can be made several hours ahead and rewarmed.

content.text: The sauce is made in two stages: the onions cook for 30 minutes over a very low heat until completely soft and sweet, almost caramelised. Then the anchovies are added and stirred until they dissolve. The anchovies must dissolve completely -- they should leave no visible pieces. Use whole wheat spaghetti if bigoli are unavailable.

items.prepNote: whole wheat spaghetti or thick spaghetti -- use bigoli if available

content.text: Heat {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} olive oil in a wide, heavy pan over the lowest possible heat. Add {{onion}} onion. Cook very slowly, stirring occasionally, for 30 minutes until completely soft, sweet, and starting to turn golden. Add {{white-wine-dry}} white wine (if using) and cook for 5 more minutes.

Add {{anchovies}} anchovies to the onion pan. Stir over very low heat until the anchovies dissolve completely into the oil -- about 3 to 4 minutes. No pieces should remain. Add {{black-pepper}} pepper. Do not add salt -- the anchovies provide all that is needed.

Cook the {{spaghetti}} pasta in well-salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve a cup of pasta water. Drain and add the pasta to the anchovy-onion sauce with a splash of pasta water. Toss well. Add {{parsley-flat}} parsley if using and serve immediately.

items.symptom: The anchovy flavour is very strong
items.cause: The anchovies were not stirred long enough to dissolve, or too many were used.
items.fix: Stir the anchovies over very low heat until they dissolve completely into the oil. A longer cooking time with more olive oil softens the flavour. The onions also moderate the sharpness -- make sure they were cooked long enough.

content.text: Bigoli in salsa is a Venetian fasting dish, eaten on days when the Church forbade meat: Christmas Eve, Good Friday, and the July feast of the Redeemer. The dish is meatless and uses only cupboard ingredients. Bigoli are made with a wooden press called a bigolaro, which was standard equipment in Venetian kitchens until the twentieth century. The dish is now served year-round and is one of the most recognised dishes of Venetian cooking.
